nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a natural number, let $\lambda(K)$ be the value of the Carmichael function at $K$, and let $R$ be the largest exponent in the prime factorization of $K$ ($R = 0$ for $K \le 1$). Then the Fubini numbers $F(n)$ satisfy $F(n + \lambda(K)) \equiv F(n) \pmod K$ for every natural number $n \ge R$.
nodes.title: Eventual periodicity of the Fubini numbers modulo $K$

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be an odd natural number and let $\lambda(K)$ be the value of the Carmichael function at $K$. Then a natural number $p$ is divisible by $\lambda(K)$ if and only if there is a natural number $N$ such that the Fubini numbers $F(n)$ satisfy $F(n + p) \equiv F(n) \pmod K$ for all $n \ge N$. In particular, the eventual period of the Fubini numbers modulo $K$ is exactly $\lambda(K)$.
nodes.title: Eventual periods of the Fubini numbers modulo an odd number

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a natural number, let $\lambda(K)$ be the value of the Carmichael function at $K$, and let $R$ be the largest exponent in the prime factorization of $K$ ($R = 0$ for $K \le 1$). Then $a^R \equiv a^{\lambda(K) + R} \pmod K$ for every natural number $a < K$.
